se-log.title: An append-only log with an in-memory index
se-log.description: A write is appended to a log file and synced to disk, the hash index records its byte offset, and a later read jumps straight to that offset.
se-log.note: Durable after the sync; findable through an index that is rebuilt after a restart.

se-lsm.title: An LSM tree's path from memory to merged files
se-lsm.description: A write enters a write-ahead log and a sorted in-memory memtable, the memtable is flushed as an immutable sorted file, and compaction later merges those files.
se-lsm.note: Writes stay cheap because no file is edited; compaction pays that debt later.

se-btree.title: A B-tree page change, protected by a log
se-btree.description: The engine changes a cached page, records the change in the write-ahead log, syncs the log at commit, and writes the page to disk later.
se-btree.note: The commit is safe once the log is synced, even though the page is still only in memory.

se-choose.title: Write amplification by engine and row size
se-choose.description: With example settings, a B-tree's write amplification falls sharply as rows grow from 100 bytes to 4 KB, while an LSM tree's stays about the same, so row size flips the winner.
se-choose.note: Assumes 16 KB pages, one changed row per page flush, and four 10x LSM levels.

se-indexes.title: What each indexing choice buys and costs
se-indexes.description: Four options compared: no index, a secondary index, a covering index, and many indexes, each with its effect on reads and writes.
se-indexes.note: Each index speeds some reads; every insert pays for all of them.

se-olap.title: Row and column storage for two kinds of query
se-olap.description: A row store handles a single-row lookup cheaply but reads everything for a scan; a column store reverses that, scanning few columns cheaply but rebuilding rows from many files.
se-olap.note: Scan sizes assume 1 billion rows of 500 bytes, and 3 columns of 8 bytes each.

items.title: Row store, lookup
items.detail: one page holds the whole row
